responses.tool-purpose: Adapts source materials into learner-friendly resources and revision tasks.
responses.problem-solved: It helps staff create accessible versions of dense academic texts more quickly.
responses.feature-interest: Using one source text to create discussion prompts and key-word support.
responses.test-request: We asked Diffit to create a simplified resource and discussion questions from a text about assessment design.
responses.test-what-happened: The tool generated a clearer reading version and a set of prompts that were usable after light editing.
responses.surprised: The vocabulary support was more useful than the discussion prompts.
responses.corrected: We removed a few repetitive questions and reworded one explanation that was slightly misleading.

strengths.text: Accessible outputs make difficult texts easier to approach.
Vocabulary and comprehension support are quick to generate.

weaknesses.text: Prompt quality can become repetitive across tasks.

opportunities.text: Can support inclusive preparation for students before class.

threats.text: There is a risk of reducing complexity too far if staff do not review carefully.

responses.learning-improve: It can lower the reading barrier for students who need a more accessible first encounter with the topic.
responses.teacher-time: Creating adapted handouts and first-draft discussion questions.
responses.avoid-use: Avoid it where nuance and original phrasing are central to the learning outcome.
responses.check-before-use: Check whether examples, simplifications, and generated questions still reflect the source accurately.

quadrant-map.rationale: It saves time and improves access, but still carries some risk if edits are skipped.

responses.ai-decisions: It decided which vocabulary needed scaffolding and which ideas to compress into a simpler explanation.
responses.human-judgement-needed: Educators need to confirm that simplification supports learning without weakening the underlying concept.
responses.concerned: A novice teacher might assume accessibility always equals accuracy and miss where subtle ideas were lost.
responses.other-educators-know: The first draft is helpful, but the educational value depends on active teacher editing.
responses.view-change: We finished more positive about its accessibility benefits, but less convinced by the originality of its prompts.
